# A Neural Link client that gave up never attaches to a later bridge

## Context

Split from #18939 on 2026-09-19. #18939 keeps the `query_component` dotted-path defect. This ticket takes its second half, whose acceptance criteria turned out to be jointly unsatisfiable as filed (measurement below).

## The Problem

An app that boots while no Neural Link bridge listens never attaches to one started later. `Neo.ai.Client`'s socket (`Neo.data.connection.WebSocket`, `maxReconnectAttempts = 5`) gives up, `Client#onSocketReconnectFailed` warns "reconnecting stopped", and nothing dials again. Observed 2026-09-18: the Portal booted with no bridge running. After the bridge started, `healthcheck` showed `sessions: []` until the tab was reloaded.

**Why "a silent slow poll" cannot be the fix — measured 2026-09-19.** In headless Chromium, a dedicated worker dialled a closed port three times with `onerror` handled. Each failed dial produced a browser-level DevTools error (CDP `Log.entryAdded`, source `worker`):

```
WebSocket connection to 'ws://127.0.0.1:9/' failed: Error in connection establishment: net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED
```

JavaScript saw nothing (no console API call), and cannot suppress the line. So any background poll prints one error per attempt in the DevTools of every developer running an app without the bridge. The public Portal is unaffected (`worker.App` skips the client when `isGitHubPages`), so the audience is local dev and dist runs.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/ai/Client.mjs#onSocketReconnectFailed`; `src/data/connection/WebSocket.mjs` (`maxReconnectAttempts`, `backoffStrategy`).
- `src/main/DomEvents.mjs#onVisibilitychange` already posts `{action: 'visibilityChange'}` to the App Worker. Its receiver, `Neo.worker.App#onVisibilityChange`, fires `visibilitychange` on that window's app only, so a worker-wide singleton like the client cannot hear it. Window `focus` is not forwarded at all.
- `src/worker/App.mjs` loads the client only when `useAiClient` matches the environment.
- `src/worker/Base.mjs` forwards every App Worker console call to the bridge while `client.isConnected` is true.

## The Fix — a fork, decided: A

| option | late-bridge attach | output with no bridge |
|---|---|---|
| **A. re-dial on visibility or focus gain** (chosen) | on the next tab switch or window focus. The observed case is covered in practice, because the operator's click from the terminal back into the browser fires `focus` | none while nobody returns to the window. Each return costs one refused dial, so one DevTools line |
| B. capped slow poll while visible | within one poll interval, no gesture | one DevTools error per attempt |
| C. both | fastest | B's lines |

**Correction to the first recommendation.** It said A "costs nothing while idle", and that B's cost falls on every developer who never uses the Neural Link. A's cost falls on those developers too, once per return to the window, and `focus` fires often: each click from DevTools back into the page is one. So returns are gated. The client dials only after its socket gave up, one dial at a time, and at most once per backoff step since the last failure. With the default strategy that is 16 s after the boot give-up and 30 s after each refused re-dial. A refused re-dial prints nothing through the console API.

**Found while implementing: losing a connected bridge floods the console, measured on `dev@ad44280df2`.** `Client#onSocketClose` logged "Disconnected" while `isConnected` was still true. The worker forwarded that line to the bridge, and a send on the closed socket starts a reconnect. That reconnect logs its attempt, which is forwarded again. Once the attempts run out, the give-up warning is forwarded the same way, and the loop runs until the stack overflows. Stopping a connected bridge produced 527 "reconnecting stopped" warnings within 3 s, plus `Duplicate event handler attached: open Socket`. Before this ticket that only happened when a connected bridge was lost. Once a late bridge can attach, every attach can end that way, so it belongs here. The first fix dropped the flag in `onSocketClose` before logging. Review of PR #18970 found the second entry: a failing socket reports `error` before `close`, and the error's own warning took the same path (537 attempts, 527 reports and a stack overflow, triggered by an invalid UTF-8 frame). So `isConnected` stopped being a flag. It reads the socket's `readyState`, and no line is ever sent through a socket that is not open, in whatever order the socket fails.

## Contract Ledger

"M" names the PR #18970 mutation row whose arm fails when that behaviour is undone.

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback / Edge Case | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Neo.main.DomEvents#onWindowFocus` (new) | option A | on window `focus`, posts `{action: 'windowFocus', data: {windowId}}` to the App Worker, in every Neo app | the listener is on `window` without capture, and `focus` does not bubble, so an element gaining focus inside the page does not fire it | JSDoc | M6 |
| `Neo.worker.App#onWindowFocus` (new) | option A | fires the worker-level event `windowFocus` with `{windowId}` | no app-level event | JSDoc | M6 |
| `Neo.worker.App#onVisibilityChange` | option A | unchanged: `hiddenTick.sync(data)`, then the app-level `visibilitychange` with `{hidden, visibilityState, windowId}`. New: the worker-level `visibilityChange` with the same payload | hidden reports are fired too; the client ignores `hidden: true` | JSDoc | M7 |
| `Neo.ai.Client#redial` (new, public) | option A + the gate above | dials only if all three hold: the socket gave up (`gaveUpAt` set), its socket is `CLOSED` (no dial in flight), and at least `socket.backoffStrategy(socket.reconnectAttempts)` ms passed since the last failure | a return inside the step does nothing and **schedules nothing**: no later retry, only the next return after the step dials. Default gap: 16 s after the boot give-up, 30 s after each refused re-dial; a custom `backoffStrategy` sets it | JSDoc | M1 · M2 · M9 |
| client output after the give-up | the `onSocketError` / `onSocketReconnectFailed` docblocks | the first give-up warns once, "reconnecting stopped until a window is focused or shown again". A refused re-dial prints nothing through the console API | the browser still writes one DevTools line per refused dial, which no script can suppress | JSDoc | M3 · M4b · M5 |
| `Neo.ai.Client#isConnected` (now a getter) | the flood above | true only while the socket's `readyState` is `OPEN`, so the worker's console forwarding and the client's own sends never reach a socket that is not open | covers `error` before `close`, `close` alone and a closing handshake alike. Nothing outside the client writes it | JSDoc | M4 · M4-dev |
| `Neo.ai.Client#onSocketClose` | — | logs "Disconnected" only when the socket had opened, which a private flag remembers | a refused dial disconnects nothing | JSDoc | M4b |
| `Neo.ai.Client#onSocketOpen` | — | clears `gaveUpAt`, so a bridge lost later is reported again and its own reconnect cycle runs first. It logs "Connected" after flushing the buffered lines, which keeps the bridge's log in order | — | JSDoc | M8 · M10 |
| `Neo.data.connection.WebSocket#onClose` | — | no longer warns "closed abnormally, attempting reconnect…"; `attemptReconnect()` logs each attempt it schedules and, after a give-up, schedules none | pre-existing and out of scope: `onClose(event, reason, wasClean)` never receives `reason` or `wasClean`, so a clean 1000 close reconnects too (defect-note 2026-09-19 14:18Z, corrected 14:18Z) | inline comment | M5 |

Unchanged: the app-level `visibilitychange` name and payload. `Neo.Main.windowFocus`, the main-thread remote that focuses a window, is unrelated to the new App Worker action of the same name.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An App Worker whose client gave up attaches to a bridge started later, without a reload, on the next visibility or focus gain.
- [ ] With no bridge, nothing is dialed or printed after the capped attempts until a user returns to a window. A return dials at most once per backoff step since the last failure, and a refused re-dial prints nothing through the console API. Measured through CDP `Log.entryAdded`, not only the console API.
- [ ] A repeated return while a dial is pending does not stack sockets.
- [ ] Losing a connected bridge is reported once when the reconnect attempts run out, with no re-entrant logging.

## Out of Scope

- #18939's `query_component` dotted paths.
- Brain-side Neural Link surfaces (neomjs/neo-agent-brain#371).
